This isn't really a rate limiter (executions / time period), but a semaphore (bounding parallel calls). Rather than implementing one informally with blocking channels, you might want to consider using https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/sync/semaphore instead.

Thundering herd disk stats collection is kinda expensive, so introducing some bounding is probably a reasonable thing to do here (because there isn't really much we can do to make it significantly cheaper).

> This isn't really a rate limiter (executions / time period), but a semaphore (bounding parallel calls). Rather than implementing one informally with blocking channels, you might want to consider using https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/sync/semaphore instead.
> 
> Thundering herd disk stats collection is kinda expensive, so introducing some bounding is probably a reasonable thing to do here (because there isn't really much we can do to make it significantly cheaper).

@endocrimes thanks, I have added semaphore

Sorry couple of silly questions.

You've set the semaphores concurrent call limit to 100. Where did we get that value from? It wasn't clear to me from the original bug how many concurrent du instances you were dealing with. Looking at the issue 100 instances of du look like it will already be using 5-10 cores. Would it make sense for this value to be configurable?

The sync.Once is part of the fsResourceAnalyzer struct so new instance of that struct will have a seperate syncOnce and a separate semaphore. So if you have multiple fsResourceAnalyzer instances your actually concurrent call limit will be a multiple of 100.  

Also if we have multiple fsResourceAnalyzer we won't take advantage of cached values computed while we were blocked. Would it make sense to see if a some other instances have gotten a value while we were blocked?
